Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply with the bat. The players of Netherlands Women huddle up near the ropes before scattering across the park. Their body language looks very positive as they spring out to take their spots on the field. Now then, Juairiya Ferdous walks along with Dilara Akter to open for Bangladesh Women. And it will be Iris Zwilling who bowls the first over. There's no slip in place for Ferdous, who is ready to face the first ball. Off we go again...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A tough challenge ahead - Indeed, for Bangladesh. While 140 hardly looks like a daunting target to chase, Bangladesh Women will need to pull off their highest successful run chase in T20 World Cup history to get there. In fact, they have chased 125 or more on just four occasions in the shortest format. So it is not going to be an easy task for them. The Netherlands Women, meanwhile, will be eager to strike early and pile on the pressure to turn this into a real contest. Can they make their T20 World Cup debut special and historic? We shall find out. The run chase is on the other side very shortly.

The captain led from the front - At 76/5 and crawling along at barely a run a ball, the Netherlands badly needed a rescue act. The de Leede name has long carried weight in Dutch cricket, and captain Babette de Leede, cousin of Bas de Leede from the men's team, stepped up to honour it. Fluency did not come easy for her either at first, but with the top order in ruins, the job of steadying the ship fell on the captain alone. Partners kept falling away around her, leaving her isolated for long periods, yet she grew steadily into her innings, anchoring one end and keeping the scoreboard ticking over. She got off to a fifty, but was run out and couldn't see through. However, precious contributions by the likes of Silver Siegers and Iris Zwilling at the backend ensured that they posted a decent total in the end.

Disciplined with the ball in the first half - The Netherlands made a jittery start, losing both openers inside the Powerplay and slipping to 48/3 once Sterre Kalis, one of their key batters, also fell. Bangladesh Women were nearly flawless with their execution, breaking partnerships at regular intervals and giving the opposition no room to hit back. Marufa Akter and Ritu Moni were tight as a drum through their spells, with the rest of the bowling unit chipping in just as effectively, while Rabeya Khan got to the milestone of completing 50 T20I wickets and was miserly too.

The Dutch finish strong - A very decent finish from Netherlands Women in the last couple of overs while batting first on their T20 World Cup debut. Surely, they will be delighted as they head back into the dressing room and their efforts are applauded by the Dutch faithful who have turned up in decent numbers. Bangladesh, on the other hand, were pretty sloppy towards the backend and would feel that they gave away a few extra runs.

The keeper, Nigar Sultana collects the throw a bit away from the sticks and flicks it onto the woodwork to catch the Dutch skipper short of her crease. She will need some support from the other end if the Netherlands are to post a competitive total. The Dutch will be hoping to get up to 140, but plenty will depend on how long de Leede can stay at the crease. Rabeya Khan returns to the attack. 2-0-14-1 so far for the leggie.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities, and the focus now shifts to the action between the bat and the ball. Nigar Sultana and her troops disperse from the huddle and head out to the middle. They are followed by the two Dutch openers, Heather Siegers and Phebe Molkenboer. Fariha Trisna will start things off with the ball. Nigar Sultana is standing up to the stumps to the left-arm medium pacer. Siegers will take strike. Off we go...

Time for the national anthems - The giant flags of both countries are unfurled in the middle. Out walk the match officials. Both captains now lead their teams out and get lined up. It will be the Dutch national anthem first, followed by that of Bangladesh.

How's the Dutch camp feeling? Sterre Kalis has caught up with Alan Wilkins. Kalis says it is really important for the players to enjoy the occasion, and she acknowledges that there has been a big build-up to the tournament. Standing out in the middle at a World Cup is a special moment, and she wants the players to take it all in and enjoy the experience. Kalis mentions that many of the Dutch players are working professionals away from cricket and have made significant sacrifices to get to this stage. Further says that there is naturally a mix of nerves and excitement within the group, but she is delighted that they are finally here. On the challenge ahead, Sterre says that the Netherlands did beat Bangladesh not too long ago, but stresses that they will need to play their best cricket. She also acknowledges the tremendous support they have received from back home, with plenty of family and friends in attendance as well, and says the team really appreciates all the support.

PITCH REPORT - Charles Dagnall and Anjum Chopra are near the deck. Charles says it is a bright, sunny morning with a gentle breeze blowing in from the southwest. Mentions that the straight boundary measures around 70 metres, while the square boundaries are 61 and 55 metres respectively. He informs that this is the same surface that was used for the Sri Lanka-England game. Anjum believes that this will be a good batting wicket and batters will enjoy the freedom of hitting through the line. Charles shares that despite it being a used surface, the pitch still looks remarkably fresh, and he feels there are plenty of runs on offer.

Netherlands Women (Playing XI) - Heather Siegers, Phebe Molkenboer, Babette de Leede (C/WK), Sterre Kalis, Robine Rijke, Sanya Khurana, Frederique Overdijk, Iris Zwilling, Caroline de Lange, Silver Siegers and Isabel Van Der Woning.

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Dilara Akter, Juairiya Ferdous, Sharmin Akhter, Nigar Sultana (C/WK), Sobhana Mostary, Shorna Akter, Ritu Moni, Rabeya Khan, Marufa Akter, Sanjida Akter Meghla and Fariha Trisna.

The captain of Bangladesh Women - Nigar Sultana says they were looking to bat as well because of the conditions. Nigar adds that they have a really good bowling unit and will be looking to restrict the opponents to a low total. Nigar mentions that the girls have worked very hard in the past few months, and this is the perfect opportunity for them to shine.

The skipper of the Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede says the outfield is pretty fast and the wicket looks very flat. Highlights that the way England batted in the first game here indicates it is a good batting surface. Says they want to bat big and defend. About the team combination, she informs that they have the same team that they won with in the Qualifier. Mentions they are super excited as it is a dream coming true for all of them in the side.
TOSS - It is a bit cloudy, but, importantly, dry at the moment. Time for the coin to go up in Birmingham. 'Tails' is the call from Babette de Leede, and she gets it right. Netherlands will BAT first.

A test of nerves - Both teams arrive at Edgbaston searching for confidence after tough warm-up results. Bangladesh lost consecutive games to Ireland and New Zealand, exposing gaps in batting depth and finishing. Netherlands fell to Scotland and Sri Lanka, leaving questions about how they handle pressure against higher-ranked opposition. Toss and team news in a bit.

Netherlands step onto the world stage - This World Cup marks a landmark moment for Netherlands Women as they make their debut on the global T20 stage. Led by Babette de Leede, the Dutch have shown clear structural growth over the last few seasons and see this tournament as proof that associate nations belong at the top table. Their core revolves around impact players. Robine Rijke and Sterre Kalis can change games with the bat, Iris Zwilling adds balance as a genuine all-rounder, and Caroline de Lange offers control with the ball. Playing as underdogs, Netherlands enter with freedom and intent. An upset here would send a statement and put them firmly in the qualification conversation.

Bangladesh bank on a balanced squad - The Tigresses arrive in England determined to make amends for their 2024 World Cup exit, where one win from four group games cut their campaign short. Under captain Nigar Sultana, they bring a bowling unit built for control and pressure. Nahida Akter and Rabeya Khan provide spin that suffocates in the middle overs, while Ritu Moni and young pace spearhead Marufa Akter are tasked with exploiting early movement in English conditions. The structure of their bowling attack looks solid, but the spotlight stays on the batting. Bangladesh need consistent, explosive starts from the top order to give their bowlers a total worth defending and to avoid the collapses that plagued them last time.

Welcome to Edgbaston - Hello and welcome to everyone tuning in as Bangladesh Women and Netherlands Women open their ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026 campaigns in Match 5 at Edgbaston. In a short, unforgiving group stage where every point and every decimal of net run rate can decide knockout fates, this fixture carries immediate weight. Both sides arrive after demanding warm-up schedules and little margin for error.
... MATCHDAY ...

Clash of the underdogs - The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 is off to an explosive start in England, bringing together 12 elite teams fighting across 33 games for ultimate glory. Match 5 features a compelling Group A clash between Bangladesh Women and Netherlands Women at Edgbaston, Birmingham. In a ruthless group featuring heavyweights like Australia, India, South Africa, and Pakistan, there is absolutely no margin for error. Tigresses' game plan - Bangladesh Women arrive at the tournament on the back of mixed results, having dominated the global qualifiers but suffering a recent Tri-Series loss against the same Dutch opponents. To assert their dominance, the Tigresses will look to unleash their powerful middle-order engine room to post an intimidating score or a clinical target. Once the runs are on the board, the strategy shifts directly to their trademark spin choke on the gripping Edgbaston track, aiming to constrict the scoring options and completely suffocate the Dutch batting line-up through defensive over-by-over pressure. Bangladesh's team combination -  Led by skipper Nigar Sultana, Bangladesh boasts a highly structured squad built around multi-dimensional players. Dynamic young batters Dilara Akter and Sobhana Mostary provide crucial fireworks, while versatile all-rounders Shorna Akter and Ritu Moni anchor the transitions between disciplines. The bowling combination is heavily reliant on a world-class spin core containing Nahida Akter, Fahima Khatun, and young Rabeya Khan. This slow-bowling arsenal is well-complemented by the raw pace of prodigy Marufa Akter, ensuring the Tigresses have a tactical answer for every stage of the game. Debutants Netherlands primed but sweating on injury - Netherlands Women arrive incredibly well-prepared for their historic, first-ever appearance at a T20 World Cup. Skipper Babette de Leede leads a fearless roster whose core strength lies in their electric fielding and an aggressive, fearless approach to batting. However, one key area they desperately need to tighten up is their death-overs bowling, which has leaked crucial runs in recent outings. Compounding this tactical worry is a major injury concern surrounding premier bowler Isabel Van Der Woning, who dramatically went down clutching her hamstring during their final warm-up fixture against Sri Lanka. Her potential absence leaves a massive void in the Dutch plans. Key matchups - The tactical battles within this fixture promise pure theatre on the pitch. In the Powerplay, a blockbuster face-off awaits as the aggressive, hard-hitting Dutch star Heather Siegers looks to take down the fiery opening spells of the Bangladesh pacers. In the middle overs, all-rounder Frederique Overdijk will be tasked with using her tight variations to break the rhythm of Bangladesh’s key middle-order anchors. The ultimate defining narrative, however, will be how the Dutch batting line-up counters the relentless turning ball of the Bangladesh spinners. Team form (Last 5 completed T20Is, recent first) - BAN-W - WWLLL | NED-W - LLWLL. Edgbaston showdown awaits - Will the Netherlands pull off a monumental, historic World Cup win to announce themselves on the global stage? Or will the spin-heavy tactical machine of Bangladesh successfully suffocate the newcomers? Expect fierce competition as both nations battle for survival in the ultimate proving ground.
